findings.title: Reader thread is never joined before asserting on caught exceptions
findings.body:
After the delete loop, the test sets `deletedAll` to true and immediately asserts that `caughtExceptions` is empty. It never waits for the reader thread to finish.

A request already in flight when the flag flips can still fail and add its exception after the assertion has run. The reader may also have completed few or no requests while the deletes were happening.

Consequences:
- The test can pass even when the NPE still occurs, so it is not a reliable regression test.
- The unjoined thread keeps calling the admin API on the shared managed realm while the next test starts.

Keep a reference to the thread, `join()` it after setting the flag, and preferably check that at least one read overlapped the deletions.

findings.title: Same NPE remains in the paginated getSubGroupsStream overloads
findings.body:
`getSubGroupsCount()` now handles `modelSupplier.get()` returning null when the group was deleted concurrently. The three `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads at lines 256, 262 and 268 still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` with no null check.

In the same race, the delegate lookup returns null and these calls throw a NullPointerException. Admin endpoints that list subgroups (for example the `/children` endpoint or hierarchy population with paging) can still fail with a 500 while groups are being deleted.

Apply the same null handling here, for example by returning `Stream.empty()` when the model is null.
